label: At most one maximum in being, from the necessary root identified with every maximum
description: The premise d6549981 supplies one n that is an actual root of the selected relation at w, exists at every world accessible from w (NECESSARY_2), is necessary per se in the tertia via's modal reading (NECESSARY_4), and is identical with every y that is maximal in being under the same InAct, MoreIn and esse (IsMaximumIn, MAXIME_ENS_1). Given maxima x and y, the identity clause gives x = n and y = n, so x = y. That is AtMostOneMaximeEns for the same InAct, MoreIn and esse. Only the identity clause is used. Its standalone form, that some n equals every maximum, is equivalent to the conclusion on an inhabited carrier and is not a separate corpus statement, so no weaker non-circular premise is available. The step does not pass between the two NECESSARY senses or the two grounding senses: the premise carries both about the same witness, from its upstream derivation (isNecessaryOfNecessaryAt, and rootness defined as having no actual concrete ground), and the proof discards those clauses. Scope: InAct and MoreIn are not world-indexed; the bridge module reads them at w, and the conclusion is about those same predicates. The argument adds a support option for 5a594b1e whose warrant runs through the necessary-root route and the tertia via convergence (the population, restricted well-foundedness and contingent-grounding premises of either producer, 6b75bdf8 globally at w or 6971850e on one selected ancestry cone, with excluded middle, the necessity-cause bridge d29cebca, d9fad785, 79281639 and 3c468121, all upstream of d6549981). It shares d9fad785 with the genus-causation support ef122ccf and replaces that argument's d5a94eb1 (a cause of a quality is more such) with the necessary-root premises. It does not assert that anything is maximal in being.
